**List Reversible MCP Writes Workflow — guide the user naturally through these steps:**

**Step 1 · Confirm rollback intent.** Use this when the user asks to undo, roll back, revert, or restore a recent MCP write action.

**Step 2 · Load recent candidates.** Call this tool to list successful MCP write actions that have explicit lossless revert support. Use `first` only when the user asks for a specific number of recent actions.

**Step 3 · Present the choices.** Show the returned writes with the target, affected fields, completed time, and whether a newer write exists for the same target. Ask which specific write the user wants to inspect before calling `revert_mcp_write_prepare`.

contra_tools.name: revert_mcp_write_prepare
contra_tools.description:
**Revert MCP Write Prepare Workflow — guide the user naturally through these steps:**

**Step 1 · Choose the write.** Ask the user which reversible write they want to inspect. Use `list_reversible_mcp_writes` first if they have not already provided a specific audit id.

**Step 2 · Prepare only.** Call this tool with the selected `auditId` to build a revert draft. This does not apply the revert.

**Step 3 · Review the preview.** Show the returned preview to the user, including the target and fields that would be restored. Wait for explicit approval before calling `revert_mcp_write_confirm`.

auditId.description: The audit id for the reversible MCP write action to prepare for revert.

contra_tools.name: revert_mcp_write_confirm
contra_tools.description:
**Revert MCP Write Confirm Workflow — guide the user naturally through these steps:**

**Step 1 · Confirm approval.** Only use this after the user has reviewed the `revert_mcp_write_prepare` preview and explicitly approved applying the revert.

**Step 2 · Apply the draft.** Call this tool with the prepared `draftId` and `confirm: true`.

**Step 3 · Report the result.** Tell the user whether the revert applied successfully and summarize the affected target from the returned result.

Once the full prompt text is ready, call this tool to prepare a preview. Show the returned preview to the user and wait for explicit approval before calling `update_co_agent_intake_prompt_confirm`.

contra_tools.name: get_user_profile_by_username
contra_tools.description:
Fetches a user profile by username, including the UserProfile ID needed for chat and inquiry flows, formal portfolio project previews, social-post-backed Work-tab items, and recent profile posts. Useful when the target user is not discoverable via search_freelancers.

Profile work content has three distinct buckets. `projectPreviews` are formal portfolio projects/case studies: they live at `/p/{slug}`, have portfolio-project fields such as cover, title, roles, tools, outcomes, collaborators, and richer case-study content, and can be inspected or edited with the portfolio project tools.

`workPostPreviews` are social-post-backed items that appear on the profile Work tab: they are posts surfaced as work, live at `/community/{socialPost.slug}`, usually contain shorter post-style text/media. They are valuable posts, contribute to the users public perception and work credibility, and simply showcase work in a less formal format than portfolio projects/case studies. Use them as Work-tab context, but do not pass their slugs to portfolio-project edit/detail tools.

`postPreviews` are recent profile Posts-tab feed items from `socialPosts(filter: { username })`: they may include general updates, work notes, replies, or community content. They are useful profile context, but they are not portfolio projects unless separately represented in `projectPreviews`.

When a user asks about portfolio projects, case studies, or related work for service attachments, prefer `projectPreviews` or `list_portfolio_projects` and `workPostPreviews` together. When a user asks about posts or Work-tab posts, include `workPostPreviews` and `postPreviews` and route them to the returned `/community/...` URLs.

**Viewing images**: This tool returns `previewUrl` links for avatar, project cover, work-post, and profile-post images.

username.description: Individual Contra profile handle or legacy account username to look up, for example "alice".

contra_tools.name: update_profile_prepare
contra_tools.description:
**Update Profile Workflow — guide the user naturally through these steps:**

**Step 1 · Identify changes.** Use the user request and profile context first. If they ask for an audit or edit, prepare the highest-impact concrete change instead of opening with a form. Supported fields: `bio` (max 2800 chars), `headline` (max 60 chars, shown as the professional title), `firstName`, `lastName`, `avatarImageUrl` (a publicly accessible image URL), `coverImageUrl` (a publicly accessible image URL for the banner / cover image displayed above the avatar), `availableForWork` (true to make the profile available/open to work; false to make it unavailable), `externalLinks` (label + URL pairs for Calendly, LinkedIn, Twitter/X, Dribbble, personal websites, and other public links), and `locationGooglePlaceId` (Google Place ID — a plain city name is not accepted). At least one field is required. Username changes are not supported here — direct the user to their settings page at contra.com/settings.

**Step 2 · External links.** If the user asks to add or set a Calendly, LinkedIn, Twitter/X, Dribbble, personal website, or other external URL, put it in `externalLinks` with a clear `label` and the public `url`. This tool preserves unrelated existing links and updates existing links with the same label, social site, or URL.

⚠️ **Roles, skills, and tools are NOT profile-level fields.** The roles, skills, and tools shown on a profile are derived from the portfolio projects and services on that profile. They cannot be edited through this tool. To change them, update the underlying portfolio project (via `update_portfolio_project_prepare`) or service that contributes the tag.

**Step 3 · Location.** If the user wants to update their location, they must supply a Google Place ID. Help them find the correct one if needed.

Never invent metrics, client names, dates, reviews, or trust claims in profile content. If the user asks for invented credibility, refuse briefly and offer honest qualitative or spec/concept framing.

Once enough information is gathered or safely assumed, call this tool to prepare a preview. Show the returned preview to the user and wait for explicit approval before calling `update_profile_confirm`.

availableForWork.description: Whether the user should be marked available/open to work on their profile. Set true to make them available for work, or false to make them unavailable.

avatarImageUrl.description: URL of the new avatar image to upload. Must be a publicly accessible image URL (JPEG, PNG, or WebP).

bio.description: Brief description shown on the profile. Max 2800 characters.

coverImageUrl.description: URL of the new profile banner / cover image to upload. Must be a publicly accessible image URL (JPEG, PNG, or WebP). Displayed as the large header image above the avatar.

externalLinks.description: External profile links to add or update. Use label + URL pairs for Calendly, LinkedIn, Twitter/X, Dribbble, personal websites, and other public links. Existing links with the same label, social site, or URL are updated; unrelated existing links are preserved.

label.description: Optional display label for the link, e.g. "Calendly", "LinkedIn", "Twitter", "Dribbble", or "Website".

url.description: Public URL to add to the profile links section.

items.description: External profile link to add or update.

firstName.description: First name displayed on the profile.

headline.description: Headline / professional title shown on the profile, e.g. "Product Designer". Max 60 characters.

lastName.description: Last name displayed on the profile.

locationGooglePlaceId.description: Google Place ID for the location to display on the profile (e.g. "ChIJOwg_06VPwokRYv534QaPC8g" for New York). The user must provide a Google Place ID; a plain city name is not accepted.

contra_tools.name: create_job_prepare
contra_tools.description:
Prepares a new standalone job and returns a preview of the hiring workspace that will create it. Uses the active unified workspace or the legacy client workspace when no workspaceId is provided.

**Job Creation Workflow — guide the user naturally through these steps:**

**Step 1 · What are you hiring for?** Ask what role or outcome the user wants to hire for. From their description, gather the core job details: `title`, `roles`, `tools`, and a plain-text `description` that is at least 250 characters long. These should be human-readable Contra role/tool names or close search terms, not raw IDs. If the match is unclear, ask a follow-up instead of guessing. Also ask whether they want to include an optional `outcomeId`.

**Step 2 · What is the budget and timeline?** Ask whether the job is fixed-price or rate-based. Use the exact budget type enums `FIXED_PRICE` or `RATE`. For rate-based budgets, use a budget interval enum of `DAY`, `HOUR`, `MONTH`, `TWO_WEEK`, `WEEK`, or `YEAR`. Also gather the budget range, whether there is an expected duration, the start timeframe using `IMMEDIATELY`, `SOON`, or `LATER`, and how many openings they want to hire for.

**Step 3 · Who should be eligible?** Ask whether the job should be limited by country, timezone overlap, language requirements, or an expert-program restriction. Only gather these fields when they matter for the role.

**Step 4 · Should the job stay private or go public?** Jobs are private by default. Ask whether the user wants the job to be public. Only set `publish: true` when they explicitly want that. If they want a public job with an external application link, also gather `externalUrl`.

**Step 5 · Anything else?** Ask whether they want to add any optional details that have not been covered yet before preparing the draft.

Once all information is gathered, call this tool to prepare the draft. Preparation selects the legacy hiring workspace when needed. Show the returned preview to the user and wait for explicit approval before calling `create_job_confirm`, which uses the previewed workspace. If they do not have a hiring workspace, the tool will return an error.

type.description: Budget type. Allowed values: FIXED_PRICE or RATE.

countryId.description: Optional GraphQL Country ID. If omitted, the job is open to all countries.

description.description: Plain-text job description. Minimum 250 characters. It will be converted into paragraphs.

duration.description: Optional job duration. Omit it for ongoing work.

externalUrl.description: Optional external application URL. Only used when publish is true; omit it to post as a Contra-exclusive job.

languages.description: Optional language requirements for the job.

numberOfOpenPositions.description: Optional number of open positions. Defaults to 1 when omitted.

publish.description: If true, publish the job after creating it. Defaults to false.

roles.description: Human-readable Contra role names or close search terms. The tool resolves them to internal role IDs during prepare. Pass an empty array when there are no specific roles yet.

startTimeframe.description: Optional desired start timeframe for the job. Allowed values: IMMEDIATELY, SOON, or LATER.

tools.description: Human-readable Contra tool names or close search terms. The tool resolves them to internal tool IDs during prepare. Pass an empty array when there are no specific tools yet.

workspaceId.description: Optional Contra workspace global ID. When provided, this workspace is used instead of the active workspace.

Show the returned preview to the user and wait for explicit approval before calling update_job_confirm.

interval.description: Budget interval. Required when budget.type is RATE. Allowed values: DAY, HOUR, MONTH, TWO_WEEK, WEEK, YEAR.

type.description: Budget type. Allowed values: FIXED_PRICE or RATE.

numberOfOpenPositions.description: Optional replacement number of open positions.

roles.description: Optional replacement Contra roles as human-readable names. Omit this field to keep the current roles unchanged.

startTimeframe.description: Optional replacement start timeframe. Allowed values: IMMEDIATELY, SOON, or LATER.

jobId.description: The existing Contra job ID. Use list_jobs first if the user does not already know it.

Show the returned preview to the user and wait for explicit approval before calling unpost_job_confirm.

jobId.description: The existing Contra job ID. Use list_jobs first if the user does not already know it.

contra_tools.description: List candidates (applicants and invited freelancers) for a specific job from the user's client workspace. Use list_jobs first to get the jobId if the user does not already know it. Supports filtering by status (e.g., show only shortlisted candidates), candidate type (applied vs. invited), and candidate source (verified Contra users, guests, or Contra picks). Results can be sorted by application date or relevance.

Use when the user says things like 'this one looks good', 'add to shortlist', 'mark as a fit', 'I like this candidate', or 'thumbs up'. Shortlisting a previously dismissed candidate automatically removes the dismissal. This action is reversible — use unshortlist_candidate to undo it.

jobCandidateId.description: The job candidate ID. Use list_job_candidates first to discover candidate IDs for a given job.

contra_tools.name: unshortlist_candidate
contra_tools.description: Remove a candidate from the shortlist, returning them to active review. Use when the user says 'remove from shortlist', 'undo fit', 'I changed my mind about this candidate', or 'un-mark as fit'. This reverses a previous shortlist_candidate action.

jobCandidateId.description: The job candidate ID. Use list_job_candidates first to discover candidate IDs for a given job.

contra_tools.name: dismiss_candidate
contra_tools.description: Mark a candidate as not a fit and remove them from active consideration. Use when the user says 'not a fit', 'pass on this one', 'reject', 'decline', 'not interested', 'thumbs down', or 'skip'. Dismissing a previously shortlisted candidate automatically removes the shortlist. This action is reversible — use undismiss_candidate to bring them back.

jobCandidateId.description: The job candidate ID. Use list_job_candidates first to discover candidate IDs for a given job.

contra_tools.name: undismiss_candidate
contra_tools.description: Restore a previously dismissed candidate back to active consideration. Use when the user says 'undo not a fit', 'give them another look', 'reconsider', 'bring back', or 'un-reject'. This reverses a previous dismiss_candidate action.

jobCandidateId.description: The job candidate ID. Use list_job_candidates first to discover candidate IDs for a given job.

contra_tools.name: respond_to_candidate_prepare
contra_tools.description:
Prepare an initial message to send to a job candidate, starting a conversation with them. Use when the user says 'message them', 'reach out', 'contact this candidate', 'get in touch', or 'send them a message'. This sends the first message only — for follow-up messages after the initial contact, use send_chat_message_prepare instead.

**Respond to Candidate Workflow — guide the user naturally through these steps:**

**Step 1 · Identify the candidate.** Determine which candidate the user wants to message. If a candidate is not already identified, use `list_job_candidates` to find them. Confirm the correct candidate with the user before proceeding.

**Step 2 · Compose the message.** Ask the user what message they want to send to the candidate. The message should be a thoughtful, personalized outreach.

**Step 3 · Prepare and preview.** Once the candidate and message are gathered, call this tool to prepare the draft. Show the returned preview to the user and wait for explicit approval before calling `respond_to_candidate_confirm`.

jobCandidateId.description: The job candidate ID. Use list_job_candidates first to discover candidate IDs for a given job.

message.description: The plain text message to send to the candidate. This will be the first message in a new conversation with them.

contra_tools.name: respond_to_candidate_confirm
contra_tools.description: Send the prepared initial message to a job candidate. Only call this after the user has explicitly approved the preview from respond_to_candidate_prepare. This creates a new chat conversation with the candidate and sends the message.

contra_tools.name: list_job_feed
contra_tools.description:
Browse and search the Contra job board (contra.com/jobs) as a freelancer. Returns paginated opportunities along with the visitor's relationship to each one (applied, bookmarked, dismissed, matched). Use this tool whenever the user asks to find jobs, browse opportunities, look for freelance work, or check bookmarked/applied jobs on Contra.

For requests to find work on Contra, search using the user's message and profile context. Search broadly from the user's message/profile context, show visible results with links and budget when available, and offer one free high-leverage next action such as improving the profile, drafting a case study, or preparing an application for a visible job.

Pick the appropriate preset based on the user's intent:
- FOR_YOU — personalized, ranked matches (the default "For You" tab on contra.com/jobs)
- ALL — every open opportunity the user can see
- APPLIED — jobs the user has already applied to
- BOOKMARKED — jobs the user saved
- NOT_A_FIT — jobs the user dismissed
- CLOSED — jobs that are no longer accepting applications

Each returned entry includes a `jobId`, a `publicUrl` for linking the user to the listing, and, when the job is posted publicly, a `jobPosting.jobPostingId`. Pass the `jobPostingId` to `apply_to_job_prepare` to apply, or the `jobId` to `bookmark_job`, `remove_job_bookmark`, or `dismiss_job_feed_entry`. Always use `publicUrl` when sharing a link to the job with the user — do not construct URLs manually.

**Access limits:** Users without a Contra Pro subscription see a limited subset of jobs (matched jobs plus a small preview of recent opportunities). When `accessLimitedFeed` is `true` in the response, results may not reflect the full Contra job board. If results are empty or sparse, check the `accessLimitGuidance` field for recommended messaging. Never lead with the Pro upsell, never state inaccessible-job counts, and mention Pro at most once only after free value has been delivered.

after.description: Pagination cursor from a previous list_job_feed response.

maxBudgetUsd.description: Optional maximum budget in whole USD.

minBudgetUsd.description: Optional minimum budget in whole USD.

roleIds.description: Optional role IDs (GraphQL Relay IDs) to filter by.

toolIds.description: Optional tool IDs (GraphQL Relay IDs) to filter by.

first.description: Number of feed entries per page. Defaults to 25.

preset.description: Which slice of the Contra job board to browse. FOR_YOU = personalized matches on contra.com/jobs, ALL = all open opportunities, APPLIED = jobs the user already applied to, BOOKMARKED = jobs the user saved, NOT_A_FIT = jobs the user dismissed, CLOSED = jobs no longer accepting applications.

search.description: Optional search text for job titles and related job content.

sort.description: Optional sort order. Defaults to NEWEST (most recently posted). MOST_RELEVANT ranks by match relevance.

contra_tools.name: bookmark_job
contra_tools.description: Save a Contra job board opportunity so the user can revisit it later from the Bookmarked tab. Use when the user says things like 'bookmark this', 'save this job', 'add to my saved jobs', or 'I want to look at this later'. The affected job moves into the BOOKMARKED preset of list_job_feed. This action is reversible — use remove_job_bookmark to undo.

jobId.description: The Contra Job ID (e.g. from a list_job_feed response).

contra_tools.name: remove_job_bookmark
contra_tools.description: Unbookmark a previously saved job on the Contra job board. Use when the user says 'unsave this job', 'remove from bookmarks', or 'I no longer want to follow this one'. The job is removed from the BOOKMARKED preset of list_job_feed.

jobId.description: The Contra Job ID (e.g. from a list_job_feed response).

contra_tools.name: dismiss_job_feed_entry
contra_tools.description: Dismiss a Contra job board opportunity and signal to Contra that it was not a fit. Use when the user says 'not a fit', 'hide this job', 'pass on this one', or 'don't show me this again'. The job moves into the NOT_A_FIT preset of list_job_feed and stops appearing in FOR_YOU. Optionally pass a short reason (e.g. 'budget too low') to improve future recommendations.

jobId.description: The Contra Job ID (e.g. from a list_job_feed response).

reason.description: Optional freeform reason the user is dismissing the job (e.g. "budget too low"). Helps improve future recommendations.

contra_tools.name: apply_to_job_prepare
contra_tools.description:
Prepares an application to a public Contra job posting and returns a draft preview. This is how freelancers apply to jobs they found via list_job_feed or get_job_by_slug.

**Apply to Job Workflow — guide the user naturally through these steps:**

**Step 1 · Identify the job posting.** If the user has not already picked a specific job, use `list_job_feed` (or `get_job_by_slug`) to find candidates first and show visible options. You need the `jobPostingId` (not the `jobId`) returned by those tools to apply.

**Step 2 · Fit gate.** Before preparing any application, compare the job's required skills/tools with the user's stated skills and portfolio projects. If the fit is weak, warn once with specifics. For batch/mass-apply requests, skip weak matches unconditionally and state why.

**Step 3 · Draft the application message.** If the user gave explicit apply/send intent, draft from the job, profile, portfolio, and thread context immediately using stated assumptions for gaps. Do not ask another form. The message should be plain text, personalized to the posting, and highlight why the user is a strong fit. Keep it under 10,000 characters.

**Step 4 · Attach portfolio by default.** Call `list_portfolio_projects` for the applying freelancer and pass relevant project `id` values in `relatedPortfolioProjectIds`. If no project is relevant, say that. Preparing without attachments requires the user to explicitly opt out in this conversation; only then set `portfolioAttachmentOptOutConfirmed: true`.

Once all information is gathered, call this tool to prepare the draft. Show the returned preview to the user and wait for explicit approval before calling `apply_to_job_confirm`.

calendarLink.description: Optional scheduling link (e.g. Calendly) to share with the client.

jobPostingId.description: The JobPosting ID to apply to. Use get_job_by_slug or list_job_feed to discover this ID; do not pass the Job ID here.

message.description: Optional application message to the client. Supports markdown links (e.g. [My Portfolio](https://example.com)) and basic formatting.

portfolioAttachmentOptOutConfirmed.description: Set true only when the user explicitly opted out of attaching portfolio projects in this conversation.

relatedPortfolioProjectIds.description: Portfolio project IDs to attach. Use the `id` values returned by list_portfolio_projects for the applying freelancer. Required by default unless portfolioAttachmentOptOutConfirmed is true.

workspaceId.description: Optional Contra workspace global ID. When provided, this workspace is used instead of the active workspace.

contra_tools.name: apply_to_job_confirm
contra_tools.description: Submits a prepared job application draft by ID via applyForJobPosting. Only call this after the user has explicitly approved the preview from apply_to_job_prepare.

contra_tools.name: list_user_reviews
contra_tools.description: Lists reviews received by a user profile, including rating, review text, relationship type, and reviewer details. Returns an aggregate review summary (average score and total count) alongside individual reviews. Use this to evaluate a freelancer's reputation and past client satisfaction. This tool is part of the Talent Discovery Workflow described in search_freelancers — use it during the deep-dive phase to assess review sentiment, client satisfaction patterns, and overall reputation for shortlisted candidates.

limit.description: Maximum number of reviews to return (1–50, default 20).

username.description: Contra username to look up reviews for, for example "alice".

contra_tools.name: list_portfolio_projects
contra_tools.description:
Fetches a freelancer's portfolio Work-tab content, split into case-study portfolio projects and social-post-backed work posts. `projects` contains case-study portfolio projects with full detail: id, slug, publishedAt, isDraft, content, roles, tools, outcomes, industries, organizations, collaborators, dates, external links, and verification status. `workPosts` contains profile work items backed by social posts; these live at `/community/{socialPost.slug}` and should not be passed to portfolio-project edit/detail tools.

`totalCount` reports the raw Work-tab portfolio connection count for the selected visibility, including social-post-backed work posts and items outside the current page; `projects.length` only counts case-study items returned on this page.

**Portfolio Project Listing Workflow — gather details in this order:**

**Step 1 · Identify the profile.** Use the Contra username to fetch projects. When coming from search results, pass the user's `displayUsername` as `username`.

**Step 2 · Choose visibility scope.** Omit `includeDrafts` or set it to `false` for normal public-discovery results. Set `includeDrafts: true` when the user asks about unpublished, hidden, or draft projects, such as "publish my drafts" or "remove this from my profile without deleting it".

**Step 3 · Inspect publish state and content type.** Each returned case-study project includes `publishedAt` and `isDraft`. Draft projects have `publishedAt: null` and `isDraft: true`; published projects have a timestamp and `isDraft: false`. Social-post-backed work items are returned separately in `workPosts` with `socialPost.url` routing data.

Use this after `search_freelancers` or `get_user_profile_by_username` to evaluate whether a freelancer's past work matches what the client is looking for. This tool is part of the Talent Discovery Workflow described in `search_freelancers` — use it during the deep-dive phase to assess project relevance, tools match, and outcome quality for shortlisted candidates. The returned `id` on each project is also the canonical identifier to pass as `relatedPortfolioProjectIds` when calling `apply_to_job_prepare`, `create_productized_service_prepare`, or `update_productized_service_prepare`.

To publish a draft project discovered here, call `update_portfolio_project_prepare` with the project's `slug` and `draft: false`, then show the preview and wait for explicit approval before confirming. To move a live project off the public profile without deleting it, call `update_portfolio_project_prepare` with `draft: true`.

includeDrafts.description: Set to true to include unpublished draft projects in the results. Defaults to false, which returns only public published projects.

limit.description: Maximum number of portfolio projects to return (1–25, default 10).

username.description: Contra username whose portfolio projects to fetch, for example "alice". Use displayUsername from search_freelancers results.

contra_tools.name: get_portfolio_project
contra_tools.description: Fetches full details for a single case-study portfolio project by its slug. Returns all project information including content, roles, tools, collaborators, and cover image. If the slug belongs to a profile social post, this tool returns a routing message instead of treating it like a case study.

slug.description: The slug of the portfolio project (from list_portfolio_projects results or the project URL).

contra_tools.name: resolve_contra_short_url
contra_tools.description: **MANDATORY FIRST STEP whenever the user provides a URL on `on.contra.com`** (with or without protocol — e.g. `https://on.contra.com/GtRQ8W`, `on.contra.com/GtRQ8W`). Resolves the short URL to its canonical `contra.com` destination URL. The short URL pathname (e.g. `GtRQ8W`) is NOT a slug — do NOT pass it to `get_portfolio_project`, `get_service_by_slug`, `get_product_by_slug`, `get_payment_link_by_slug`, `get_job_by_slug`, or `get_user_profile_by_username`. Always call this tool first to get the real `contra.com` URL, then extract the slug or username from that URL. For URLs that are already on `contra.com`, do NOT call this tool — extract the slug or username directly from the URL and call the appropriate existing tool. After this tool returns, examine the returned `destinationUrl` and call the matching tool: e.g. `contra.com/p/<slug>` → `get_portfolio_project`, `contra.com/<username>` → `get_user_profile_by_username`, `contra.com/s/<slug>` → `get_service_by_slug`, `contra.com/products/<slug>` → `get_product_by_slug`, `contra.com/payment-link/<slug>` → `get_payment_link_by_slug`, `contra.com/opportunity/<slug>` → `get_job_by_slug`. If the destination URL pattern is unfamiliar, fall back to telling the user the canonical link and asking how they want to proceed.

url.description: A Contra short URL to resolve. Must be on `on.contra.com` — any other URL will be rejected. Examples: `https://on.contra.com/abc123`, `on.contra.com/abc123`.

contra_tools.name: create_portfolio_project_prepare
contra_tools.description:
Prepares a new portfolio project for creation on your Contra profile and returns a draft preview. Inline images in markdown content (![alt](url)) are automatically uploaded during prepare. Standalone Vimeo and YouTube URLs placed on their own line are embedded inline in the project body. All image URLs must be publicly accessible — local file paths and base64 are not supported.

**Portfolio Project Creation Workflow — guide the user naturally through these steps:**

**Step 1 · Project title.** Ask for the project title (max 64 chars).

**Step 2 · Project content.** Ask for the project description/content. Supports markdown or plain text. To embed an inline video, place a supported provider URL on its own line; supported providers are Vimeo and YouTube (including youtu.be links, Shorts, and live video URLs).

**Step 3 · Integrity check.** Never invent performance metrics, client names, project dates, reviews, earnings, or quantified outcomes. Spec, concept, or fictional work must be labeled as spec/concept in the title or content. Refuse to publish fictional work presented as client work.

**Step 4 · Cover image.** Ask for a cover image URL. Must be a publicly accessible http/https URL. This is required when publishing immediately, but optional when creating as a draft (`draft: true`). Drafts without a cover image can add one later via `update_portfolio_project_prepare` before publishing.

**Step 5 · Roles.** Ask for the roles performed on this project (1–3 roles, max 48 characters each).

**Step 6 · Tools used.** Ask for the tools used on this project (1–5 tools, max 48 characters each).

**Step 7 · Optional details.** Ask if the user wants to add collaborators, organizations, industries, project dates (start/end), or an external link. Explain that confirming a project with collaborators sends collaboration invitation emails, and existing Contra users also receive notifications. These invitations cannot be recalled. For organizations, each entry must be `{ name, url }` — the API requires a real public http/https URL for every organization (e.g. `{ name: "Contra", url: "https://contra.com" }`). If the user cannot provide a URL for an organization, do NOT add it; ask them to skip it instead.

**Step 8 · Publish state.** Ask whether to publish the project immediately or save it as a draft. Map the answer to the `draft` field: `draft: false` (or omit) publishes immediately; `draft: true` saves as an unpublished draft hidden from the public portfolio. Drafts can be published later via `update_portfolio_project_prepare` with `draft: false`.

Once all information is gathered, call this tool to prepare the draft.

**MANDATORY preview display — before calling `create_portfolio_project_confirm`, you MUST show the user every row from the returned `preview.summary` array so they have full understanding of what will be created.** Each row is a `{ label, value }` pair already formatted for humans in plain language. Present them as a simple list, preserving the order, using the `label` text verbatim. Do NOT invent your own field names, do NOT use camelCase identifiers, do NOT skip rows whose value reads as "None" / "Not specified" — those empty values are intentional and help the user confirm that no data is missing. Only call `create_portfolio_project_confirm` after the user has explicitly approved this summary.

collaborators.description: Collaborators on this project. Each needs firstName, lastName, emailAddress, and roles.

roles.description: Roles of the collaborator on this project.

content.description: The body content of the portfolio project. Accepts markdown or plain text. Inline images using markdown syntax (![alt](url)) will be automatically uploaded. Standalone Vimeo and YouTube URLs placed on their own line (plain URL or markdown link) will be embedded inline. URLs must be publicly accessible.

coverImageUrl.description: A publicly accessible URL to the cover image for this project. Must be a valid http/https URL — local file paths and base64 data are not supported. Required when publishing immediately; optional when creating as a draft (draft: true). Drafts without a cover image can add one later via update_portfolio_project_prepare before publishing.

description.description: Short description / tagline for the project (max 300 chars). Auto-derived from content if omitted.

draft.description: Controls whether the new project is published immediately or saved as a draft. Set to true to create as an unpublished draft (hidden from the public portfolio until later published). Omit or set to false to publish immediately (default). This is the ONLY field that controls publish/draft state.

endedAt.description: Project end date in YYYY-MM-DD format.

externalLinkUrl.description: URL to an external project link (e.g. live site, Dribbble shot).

industries.description: Industry category names (e.g. "Technology", "SaaS"). Resolved to Contra industry categories.

organizations.description: Organizations / companies associated with this project. Each entry must be `{ name, url }`. The API requires a real public http/https URL for every organization — if the user cannot provide one, do NOT add the organization at all (omit it from the list).

url.description: Public website for the organization (must be a valid http/https URL). Required by the API — if the user cannot provide one, do NOT add the organization.

roles.description: Your roles on this project (1–3 roles, max 48 chars each). E.g. "Brand Designer", "Art Director".

startedAt.description: Project start date in YYYY-MM-DD format.

title.description: Title of the portfolio project (max 64 chars).

tools.description: Tools / skills used on this project (1–5 tools, max 48 chars each). E.g. "Figma", "React".

workspaceId.description: Optional Contra workspace global ID. When provided, this workspace is used instead of the active workspace.

contra_tools.name: create_portfolio_project_confirm
contra_tools.description: Confirms and creates a portfolio project from a draft prepared by create_portfolio_project_prepare. Publishes the project unless it was prepared as an unpublished draft. Adding collaborators sends collaboration invitation emails, and existing Contra users also receive notifications. These invitations cannot be recalled. Requires a draftId, confirm: true, and explicit user approval of the preview and collaborator invitations.

contra_tools.name: update_portfolio_project_prepare
contra_tools.description:
Prepares an update to an existing portfolio project by slug and returns a draft preview. Only provided fields are changed — omitted fields remain unchanged. If content or coverImageUrl are provided, images are uploaded during prepare. Standalone Vimeo and YouTube URLs placed on their own line are embedded inline in the project body. Inline media.contra.com image URLs can be reused directly; other image URLs must be publicly accessible.

📢 **Publish/draft state is controlled by the `draft` field ONLY.** The project's publish state (visible on the public portfolio vs. hidden as a draft) is stored internally as a `publishedAt` timestamp, but the user-facing control is the `draft` boolean. Set `draft: true` to move a live project back to draft, set `draft: false` to publish a draft project, or OMIT the field to leave the current publish state exactly as it is. Updating any other field (title, content, roles, etc.) without setting `draft` will NOT change the publish state — existing drafts stay drafts, existing live projects stay live.

⚠️ **FULL-REPLACEMENT FIELDS — BE CAREFUL.** The following fields behave as **full replacements** when provided: `roles`, `tools`, `collaborators`, `organizations`, `industries`, and `content`. Passing a list for any list field replaces the entire existing list on the project, **silently removing anything not included**. Passing `content` replaces the entire project body. To add a single list item, you MUST include every existing item plus the new one. To add an inline image or supported video embed to existing content, you MUST fetch the current project first and pass the complete final content body, preserving the saved text and inserting the markdown image block or standalone video URL in the requested section. To preserve a field, OMIT it entirely from the update. All other fields (`title`, `description`, `coverImageUrl`, `externalLinkUrl`, `startedAt`, `endedAt`, `draft`) use partial-update semantics — omitting means "don't change this".

**Portfolio Project Update Workflow — guide the user naturally through these steps:**

**Step 1 · Identify the project.** Identify the portfolio project to update. Call `get_portfolio_project` with the slug to load the current state — you will need the existing values for the preview diff, to construct full-replacement lists, and to preserve existing body text when updating `content`.

**Step 2 · Gather changes.** Ask which fields the user wants to change and collect the new values.

**Step 3 · Assemble full-replacement values carefully.** If the user wants to change `roles`, `tools`, `collaborators`, `organizations`, or `industries`, combine their requested changes with the existing values from step 1 to form the complete final list. Never pass a partial list — the API treats any list you send as the full desired state. If the user wants to add or move an inline image or supported video embed in the project body, build the complete final `content` value from the current project content plus the markdown image block or standalone video URL; never send only the image markdown or video URL unless the user truly wants to replace the entire body with just that media.

Once all information is gathered, call this tool to prepare the draft.

**MANDATORY preview display — before calling `update_portfolio_project_confirm`, you MUST show the user every row from the returned `preview.changes` array so they have full understanding of what is changing.** Each row is a `{ label, from, to, note? }` object already formatted for humans in plain language:

- `label` — the human-readable field name (use verbatim, do NOT replace with camelCase identifiers).
- `from` — the current value on the existing project.
- `to` — the new value that will be applied.
- `note` — (when present) a warning explaining which items will be REMOVED for full-replacement fields. Always show the note verbatim when present.

Present each row as a simple "LABEL: from → to" line, followed by the note on a new line if present. Do NOT invent field names, do NOT use camelCase, do NOT skip any row. If `preview.changes` is empty, there is nothing to apply — tell the user and do not call confirm. If `preview.warning` is a string, surface it prominently above the change list so the user sees it before the diff. Only call `update_portfolio_project_confirm` after the user has explicitly approved the full change list.

collaborators.description: FULL REPLACEMENT. If provided, this becomes the complete set of collaborators on the project — any existing collaborator not in this list will be REMOVED. Omit to preserve the current collaborators unchanged. To add one new collaborator, include every existing collaborator plus the new one; use `get_portfolio_project` to fetch the current list first.

roles.description: Roles of the collaborator on this project.

content.description: FULL REPLACEMENT. Updated body content (markdown or plain text). Inline images using markdown syntax (![alt](url)) will be automatically uploaded. Standalone Vimeo and YouTube URLs placed on their own line (plain URL or markdown link) will be embedded inline. Inline media.contra.com image URLs can be reused directly; other URLs must be publicly accessible. Omit to preserve the current content. To add an image or video embed to existing content, fetch the project first and pass the complete final body text with the markdown image or standalone video URL inserted.

coverImageUrl.description: A publicly accessible URL to the new cover image. Must be a valid http/https URL — local file paths and base64 data are not supported. Omit to preserve the current cover.

description.description: Updated short description / tagline (max 300 chars). Omit to preserve the current description.

draft.description: Controls the project's publish/draft state. Set to true to unpublish a live project (move it back to draft). Set to false to publish a draft project. Omit to preserve the current publish state unchanged — the API will NOT touch the publish timestamp on unrelated field updates. This is the ONLY field that controls publish/draft state; all other updates leave the state as-is.

endedAt.description: Updated end date in YYYY-MM-DD format. Omit to preserve.

externalLinkUrl.description: Updated external project link URL. Omit to preserve the current link.

industries.description: FULL REPLACEMENT. If provided, this becomes the complete set of industry category names — any existing industry not in this list will be REMOVED. Omit to preserve the current industries unchanged.

organizations.description: FULL REPLACEMENT. If provided, this becomes the complete set of organizations / companies on the project — any existing organization not in this list will be REMOVED. Each entry must be `{ name, url }` with a real public http/https URL — the API rejects organizations without URLs, so if the user cannot provide one, do NOT add the organization. Omit the whole field to preserve the current organizations unchanged. To add one new organization, include every existing organization plus the new one; use `get_portfolio_project` to fetch the current list first.

url.description: Public website for the organization (must be a valid http/https URL). Required by the API — if the user cannot provide one, do NOT add the organization.

roles.description: FULL REPLACEMENT. If provided, this becomes the complete set of roles on the project (1–3 roles, max 48 chars each) — any existing role not in this list will be REMOVED. Omit to preserve the current roles unchanged.

slug.description: The slug of the portfolio project to update.

startedAt.description: Updated start date in YYYY-MM-DD format. Omit to preserve.

title.description: Updated title (max 64 chars). Omit to preserve the current title.

tools.description: FULL REPLACEMENT. If provided, this becomes the complete set of tools/skills on the project (1–5 tools, max 48 chars each) — any existing tool not in this list will be REMOVED. Omit to preserve the current tools unchanged.

contra_tools.name: update_portfolio_project_confirm
contra_tools.description: Confirms and applies a portfolio project update from a draft prepared by update_portfolio_project_prepare. Overwrites supplied fields and can publish or unpublish the project. Adding collaborators sends collaboration invitation emails, and existing Contra users also receive notifications. These invitations cannot be recalled. Requires a draftId, confirm: true, and explicit user approval of the preview and any collaborator invitations. The response includes the current slug and projectUrl after the update; use those returned values for any later portfolio project calls because title changes can change the slug.

contra_tools.name: delete_portfolio_project_prepare
contra_tools.description: Prepares deletion of a portfolio project. Returns a preview of the project that will be deleted. The user must explicitly approve before calling delete_portfolio_project_confirm.

slug.description: The slug of the portfolio project to delete.

contra_tools.name: delete_portfolio_project_confirm
contra_tools.description: Confirms and executes the deletion of a portfolio project. Requires a draftId from delete_portfolio_project_prepare. This action is irreversible.

contra_tools.name: start_portfolio_site_import
contra_tools.description:
Starts Contra's portfolio site import workflow for the authenticated user. Use this when the user asks to import, pull in, migrate, or browse a public portfolio website into their Contra portfolio. Do not use generic web fetch/search for this workflow.

**Portfolio Site Import Workflow — guide the user naturally through these steps:**

**Step 1 · Source URLs.** Ask for one or more public portfolio URLs (personal site, Behance, Dribbble, etc.). Only http/https URLs are accepted.

**Step 2 · Import scope.** If the user specifies only a subset, set `importAllProjects: false`; otherwise use the default `true` so the product import flow can discover project pages from the supplied site.

contra_tools.name: create_productized_service_prepare
contra_tools.description:
Prepares a new productized service (a freelancer's offered service) and returns a draft preview. The authenticated user must be an independent/contractor.

**Productized Service Creation Workflow — guide the user naturally through these steps:**

**Step 1 · What service are you offering?** Ask for a `title` and a `description`. A great service `title` is concise (max 70 chars), outcome-driven, and names the deliverable (e.g. "Framer Landing Page in 7 Days"). The `description` accepts markdown or plain text and should explain what the buyer gets, who it's for, what makes the offering unique, and the process the user will follow. Encourage the user to include scope, process, and expected outcomes — vague descriptions hurt conversion.

**Step 2 · What does the buyer receive?** Ask for the list of `deliverables`. Each deliverable needs a concrete `title` (e.g. "Figma source file", "Production-ready Framer site") and a short `description` explaining what the buyer receives. Strong services list 2–6 specific deliverables — vague or empty deliverables hurt trust.

**Step 3 · How long does it take?** Ask for the expected delivery `duration`. `duration.amount` is a positive integer; `duration.interval` must be `DAY` or `WEEK`. Realistic durations build trust — encourage the user to set what they actually deliver, not aspirational numbers. This field is optional but strongly recommended.

**Step 4 · How much does it cost?** Ask for the `price`. Set `price.type` to exactly one of `FIXED_PRICE`, `RATE`, or `CONTACT_FOR_PRICING`. `FIXED_PRICE` requires a positive `amount` in USD. `RATE` requires both `amount` and an `interval` enum (`HOUR`, `DAY`, `WEEK`, or `MONTH`). `CONTACT_FOR_PRICING` should omit `amount` and `interval`. Optional `timeline` is a short human-readable string (e.g. "starting at"). Pricing is required to create a service.

**Step 5 · Anticipate buyer questions.** Ask whether to include `faqs`. Strong FAQs anticipate common buyer questions about turnaround, revisions, scope, eligibility, communication cadence, and what happens if expectations aren't met. Each FAQ needs a `question` and an `answer`. Up to 20 FAQs. This field is optional.

**Step 6 · Tags for discovery.** Ask whether to include `tags`. Tags are used for discovery on Contra and should be human-readable role or tool names (e.g. "Web Design", "Framer", "Backend Development"). Up to 10 tags. This field is optional but strongly recommended for visibility.

**Step 7 · Cover image.** Ask whether to include a `coverImageUrl`. This must be a publicly accessible `http(s)` URL — local paths and base64 are not supported. The image is uploaded to Cloudinary and used as the service cover. Strong covers are visual examples of the deliverable (e.g. a screenshot of the finished site, a mockup, or branded artwork). Inline markdown images inside `description` are also auto-uploaded. This field is optional but strongly recommended for engagement.

**Step 8 · Related work / case studies.** Ask whether to attach existing portfolio projects as related work. If yes, call `list_portfolio_projects` for the authenticated freelancer and pass the selected project `id` values as `relatedPortfolioProjectIds`. If a project the user names is not in the response, mention that and skip it. Omit this field or pass an empty array when the service should have no related work.

**Step 9 · Publish now or save as draft?** Ask whether to publish the service immediately. Defaults to `false` (saved as draft) so the user can review the live URL before going public. Set `publish: true` only when the user explicitly wants the service to be discoverable right away.

**Integrity and pricing guardrails.** Never invent client names, metrics, reviews, earnings, dates, or quantified outcomes for the service. If the price is pathologically low for the scope (for example a few-dollar logo or a very low monthly retainer), flag the market signal once in the preview and offer a market-rate alternative, then respect the user's choice.

Once all information is gathered, call this tool to prepare the draft.

**MANDATORY preview display — before calling `create_productized_service_confirm`, you MUST show the user every row from the returned `preview.summary` array so they have a complete picture of what will be created.** Each row is a `{ label, value }` object already formatted for humans in plain language:

- `label` — the human-readable field name (use verbatim, do NOT replace with camelCase identifiers).
- `value` — the formatted value that will be saved.

Present each row as a simple "LABEL: value" line. Do NOT invent field names, do NOT use camelCase, do NOT skip any row. Only call `create_productized_service_confirm` after the user has explicitly approved the full summary.

contra_tools.name: update_productized_service_prepare
contra_tools.description:
Prepares an update to an existing productized service (a freelancer's offered service) and returns a draft preview. Only fields explicitly provided are changed — all omitted fields are left exactly as they are. Updates are atomic in that sense: changing one field never silently mutates another.

📢 **Publish/draft state is controlled by the `publish` field ONLY.** Set `publish: true` to move a draft service live, set `publish: false` to revert a live service back to draft, or OMIT the field to leave the current publish state exactly as it is. Updating any other field (title, description, pricing, etc.) without setting `publish` will NOT change visibility — drafts stay drafts and live services stay live.

⚠️ **FULL-REPLACEMENT FIELDS — BE CAREFUL.** The following fields behave as **full replacements** when provided: `deliverables`, `faqs`, `tags`, and `relatedPortfolioProjectIds`. Passing a list for any of these replaces the entire existing list on the service, **silently removing anything not included**. To add a single item, you MUST include every existing item plus the new one. To detach all related work / case studies, pass `relatedPortfolioProjectIds: []`. To preserve the current list, OMIT the field entirely from the update. All other fields (`title`, `description`, `coverImageUrl`, `price`, `duration`, `publish`) use partial-update semantics — omitting means "don't change this".

**Productized Service Update Workflow — guide the user naturally through these steps:**

**Step 1 · Identify the service and load its current state.** Confirm which service the user wants to update. If they don't already know the `slug`, call `list_services` first and present the matches. Before gathering changes, call `get_service_by_slug` to load the current title, description, deliverables, FAQs, pricing, duration, tags, and related work — you will need these existing values to construct full-replacement lists and to confirm the diff with the user.

**Step 2 · Gather changes.** Ask which fields the user wants to change and collect the new values. Only collect fields the user actually wants to change.

**Step 3 · Assemble full-replacement lists carefully.** If the user wants to change `deliverables`, `faqs`, `tags`, or `relatedPortfolioProjectIds`, combine their requested changes with the existing values from Step 1 to form the complete final list. Never pass a partial list — the API treats any list you send as the full desired state. For related work, call `list_portfolio_projects` for the authenticated freelancer and pass the selected project `id` values. Pass `relatedPortfolioProjectIds: []` only when the user explicitly wants to detach all related portfolio projects.

**Step 4 · Pricing format.** When updating `price`, set `price.type` to exactly one of `FIXED_PRICE`, `RATE`, or `CONTACT_FOR_PRICING`. `FIXED_PRICE` requires a positive `amount` in USD. `RATE` requires both `amount` and an `interval` enum (`HOUR`, `DAY`, `WEEK`, or `MONTH`). `CONTACT_FOR_PRICING` should omit `amount` and `interval`.

**Step 5 · Duration format.** `duration.amount` is a positive integer; `duration.interval` must be `DAY` or `WEEK`.

**Step 6 · Cover image.** `coverImageUrl` must be a publicly accessible `http(s)` URL — local paths and base64 are not supported. Providing this URL replaces the existing cover; omit it to keep the current cover unchanged. Inline markdown images inside an updated `description` are also auto-uploaded to Cloudinary.

**Integrity and pricing guardrails.** Never invent client names, metrics, reviews, earnings, dates, or quantified outcomes for the service. If the requested price is pathologically low for the scope (for example a few-dollar logo or a very low monthly retainer), flag the market signal once in the preview and offer a market-rate alternative, then respect the user's choice.

Once all information is gathered, call this tool to prepare the draft.

**MANDATORY preview display — before calling `update_productized_service_confirm`, you MUST show the user every row from the returned `preview.changes` array so they have full understanding of what is changing.** Each row is a `{ label, from, to, note? }` object already formatted for humans in plain language:

- `label` — the human-readable field name (use verbatim, do NOT replace with camelCase identifiers).
- `from` — the current value on the existing service.
- `to` — the new value that will be applied.
- `note` — (when present) a warning explaining which items will be REMOVED for full-replacement fields. Always show the note verbatim when present.

Present each row as a simple "LABEL: from → to" line, followed by the note on a new line if present. Do NOT invent field names, do NOT use camelCase, do NOT skip any row. If `preview.changes` is empty, there is nothing to apply — tell the user and do not call confirm. If `preview.warning` is a string, surface it prominently above the change list so the user sees it before the diff. Only call `update_productized_service_confirm` after the user has explicitly approved the full change list.

contra_tools.name: search_freelancers
contra_tools.description:
Searches freelancers via discoverSearch (INDEPENDENTS view). Supports roles, skills/tools, expert, location, and language filters. Authenticated searches record inferred role, tool, and industry interests for Contra feed personalization.

**Talent Discovery Workflow — optimize for value before intake.**

**Exact person lookup:** If the user asks for a specific person by name, username, or @handle (for example "find Jason Obeid" or "@jason"), pass that literal name or handle in `query` and avoid adding role, tool, location, industry, or language filters unless the user also explicitly asks for them.

**Phase 1 · Search first:** For requests to find freelancers on Contra, search with the filters available from the user's words, thread context, and profile context. Do not ask for budget, timeline, tools, or industry before the first search. If details are missing, search broadly and state the assumption after results.

**Phase 2 · Teaser results:** Present 3-5 usable results with profile links, rate/price data when available, and one-line evidence. Do not show inaccessible counts or a long internal pre-filter list. After the teaser, ask at most two refining questions and include an escape hatch such as "or I can go deeper on these now." If the user gave a full brief, skip questions.

**Phase 3 · Pre-filter:** Using the search results' surface-level signals — review averages, relevant tags, title, expert badge, project previews, rate/price fit, and budget fit when supplied — select the top 8-10 candidates most likely to match. Filter hard on a stated budget; if supply does not exist at that budget, say so and offer the job-post path instead of mismatched picks.

**Phase 4 · Deep-dive (mandatory before presenting finalists):** For EACH pre-filtered candidate, you MUST call `list_portfolio_projects` (with their `displayUsername`) AND `list_user_reviews` (with their `displayUsername`). Do NOT skip this step. Evaluate each candidate against the user's requirements using these signals, weighted by what matters most to the user: relevance of past projects to the user's domain or industry, match between the candidate's tools/tech and the project's needs, quality and recency of outcomes in portfolio projects, review sentiment and client satisfaction patterns, whether portfolio projects are verified, and recency of work. Discard candidates whose portfolio and reviews do not demonstrate a strong match.

**Phase 5 · Present finalists:** Present ~3-5 finalists with a short rationale for each. Every rationale MUST reference specific portfolio projects and specific reviews — not just surface-level profile data. Include rate/price data where available. End with one concrete proposed default action, usually drafting inquiries to the top 3 or the candidates the user named.

**Viewing images**: This tool returns `previewUrl` links for avatar and project cover images.

**CRITICAL REMINDER: Do NOT present any finalist candidate without first having called `list_portfolio_projects` and `list_user_reviews` for that candidate. Skipping the deep-dive phase produces shallow, unreliable recommendations.**

expert.description: Filters by users that have at least one expert badge.

locations.description: Plain place names or serialized Discover location values. Plain names such as "New York" or "United States" are resolved automatically.

contra_tools.name: search_studios
contra_tools.description:
Searches Contra Studios — the vetted directory of studios at https://contra.com/studios. Studios are hand-vetted creative teams and agencies on Contra, suited for projects that merit more than a single freelancer.

**When to use this instead of search_freelancers:** the project spans multiple disciplines (e.g. brand + website + motion), needs parallel workstreams or more capacity than one person can deliver, calls for an end-to-end engagement with one accountable partner, or the user explicitly asks for a studio, agency, or team. For solo-scoped, single-discipline work, use search_freelancers instead. When scope is ambiguous, you may search both and present the trade-off.

**Filtering by discipline:** every response includes `availableCategories` — the studio directory categories with their slugs. Pass a slug as `categorySlug` to narrow results to one discipline. Free-text `query`, `locations`, and `languages` filters are also supported.

**Evaluating studios:** studios are Contra profiles like freelancers. Follow the same Talent Discovery Workflow described in search_freelancers: search first, show teaser results, pre-filter on surface signals, deep-dive each shortlisted studio with `list_portfolio_projects` and `list_user_reviews` (using its `displayUsername`) before presenting finalists, then propose one default next action. Clients reach out through `send_inquiry_prepare` using the studio's `userProfileId`. A studio's public profile is https://contra.com/{displayUsername}.

categorySlug.description: Studio directory category slug to narrow results by discipline. Valid slugs are returned in availableCategories on every search_studios response.

locations.description: Plain place names or serialized Discover location values. Plain names such as "New York" or "United States" are resolved automatically.

contra_tools.name: send_inquiry_prepare
contra_tools.description:
**Client Inquiry Workflow — prepare a draft before sending.**

**Step 1 · Identify the recipient.** Use the freelancer or studio's `userProfileId` from search results or profile lookup. Do not guess ids.

**Step 2 · Pick the inquiry path.** Use an existing `jobId` when the user references one, `productizedServiceId` for a service inquiry, or `jobInput` for a new scoped outreach draft. For new scoped outreach, include `jobInput` only when budget and duration are known or can be safely assumed and stated in the preview.

**Step 3 · Draft from context.** When the user explicitly says to send, contact, or apply outreach, draft immediately from thread context and stated assumptions instead of asking another form. Keep the message within Contra's 1,500 character inquiry limit.

Once the draft is ready, call this tool. Show the returned preview to the user and wait for one explicit approval before calling `send_inquiry_confirm`.

contra_tools.name: send_paid_project_proposal_prepare
contra_tools.description:
Prepares a paid project proposal and returns a draft preview. The proposal creates the project terms, generates a contract, and signs it on behalf of the authenticated user. Show the returned preview to the user and wait for explicit approval before calling send_paid_project_proposal_confirm.

**Send Paid Project Proposal Workflow — guide the user naturally through these steps:**

**Step 1 · Use context first.** If the user clicks "Send a proposal" or says to send/draft a proposal, fetch recent project/message/client context and prepare the best draft you can from that context. Do not open with "Who is this for?" when there is a likely recipient. If the recipient is unclear after context lookup, ask one concise disambiguating question.

**Step 2 · Who is the other party?** Determine who the proposal is for. If they are an existing Contra user, use `get_user_profile_by_username` to get their userProfileId. Otherwise, ask for their email, first name, and last name. Also determine the recipient's role: CONTRACTOR (if the user is hiring) or CLIENT (if the user is proposing work to a client).

**Step 3 · Project details and assumptions.** Use the thread/project context for title, scope, start date, and end date. If a value is missing but inferable, state the assumption in the preview rather than asking a separate intake round.

**Step 4 · Payment structure.** Ask which payment type the user wants only if it is not already clear: FIXED_PRICE (one lump sum with optional upfront percentage), HOURLY_RATE (pay per hour worked), or MILESTONE (split into milestones with individual amounts and due dates). Then gather the specific details:
- **FIXED_PRICE**: total amount (USD), upfront payment percentage (0-100), end date, and at least one deliverable (title + description).
- **HOURLY_RATE**: hourly rate (USD), end date, maximum hours per submission, and at least one deliverable (title + description).
- **MILESTONE**: at least one milestone, each with a title, amount (USD), and due date. Optionally a description per milestone.

**Step 5 · Fee allocation.** Ask who should cover the Contra platform fee and the payment processing fee only if missing. For each: PAYER means the client pays, RECIPIENT means the contractor absorbs it.

**Step 6 · Contract signing.** Ask for the signatory's full legal name (minimum 3 characters) only if not already known. Optionally ask if they are signing on behalf of a company — if so, collect the company name and the signatory's job title. Ask if a country-specific contract template is needed (defaults to STANDARD_AGREEMENT).

Before preparing proposals with unusually low pricing, flag the market signal once in the preview and offer a market-rate alternative. Never invent scope, credentials, metrics, or client facts to make the proposal stronger.

Once all information is gathered, call this tool to prepare the proposal draft. Show the returned preview to the user and wait for explicit approval before calling `send_paid_project_proposal_confirm`.

**Step 1 · Which product?** Ask which product the user wants to purchase. If the user has a product URL or slug, call `get_product_by_slug` (no seller username needed). Otherwise call `list_products` for the seller's username, or `get_service_by_slug` for a productized service. If the product has multiple offerings, ask the user which one to buy before continuing, and use that offering's `paymentLinkSlug`.

**Step 2 · Which payment method?** Call `list_payment_methods` to get the user's saved payment methods. If there is only one, confirm it with the user. If there are multiple, ask which one to use.

**Step 3 · Email sharing consent?** Ask whether the user consents to sharing their email address with the seller.

Once all information is gathered, call this tool to prepare the checkout draft.

**After this tool returns, you MUST:**

2. Show the agreement to the user **verbatim**: render `preview.agreement.markdown` exactly as returned. Do not paraphrase, summarize, or omit any line.
3. Ask the user explicitly whether they agree to the terms and want to proceed with the payment.
4. Only call `buy_product_confirm` after the user replies in the affirmative. Pass the user's literal approval message as `acceptanceText` (do not paraphrase — this is recorded as click-wrap consent).

contra_tools.name: create_invoice_prepare
contra_tools.description:
Prepares a new standalone invoice to send to a client and returns a draft preview. The authenticated user must be an independent/contractor.

**Invoice Creation Workflow — guide the user naturally through these steps:**

**Step 1 · Use context first.** If the user clicks "Send an invoice" or explicitly asks you to send/draft an invoice, use the thread, project, client, and account context first and prepare the best draft you can from that context. Do not open with a form when the likely client, work, line items, or due date are already known. State any assumptions in the preview.

**Step 2 · Who is this invoice for?** If the client is still unclear, ask one concise disambiguating question. Ask for their email address — the tool will automatically check if they have a Contra account. If they do, their name is resolved automatically. If they do not, you will need to ask for their first and last name (and optionally their company name). Alternatively, if you already know their Contra username, use `get_user_profile_by_username` to get their `userProfileId` and pass that instead of email.

**Step 3 · What is this invoice for?** Ask what work or services the invoice covers only if it is missing. From the user's description, build line items — each needs a description, quantity, and rate. For example, if they say "10 hours of design work at $150/hr", that becomes one line item. Confirm the items and total with the user.

**Step 4 · When is payment due?** Ask if the invoice should be due immediately upon receipt, or if there is a specific due date only when it is not inferable.

**Step 5 · Who covers the fees?** Contra charges a platform fee and a payment processing fee. Ask the user whether they (the contractor) want to absorb these fees, or if the client should pay them only when missing. Explain the options clearly.

**Step 6 · Anything else?** Ask if they want to add a memo or note to the invoice, and whether they want to set a custom invoice number (otherwise one will be auto-generated).

Once all information is gathered, call this tool to prepare the draft. Show the returned preview to the user and wait for explicit approval before calling `create_invoice_confirm`.

contra_tools.name: send_direct_payment_prepare
contra_tools.description:
Prepares a one-off / bulk direct payment to one or more freelancers using a saved payment method, and returns a draft preview with the full fee breakdown. Direct payment sends money straight to recipients (creating a paid project and invoice per recipient) — it is not tied to an existing invoice or product. The authenticated user must be acting from a client/hiring workspace with a saved payment method.

**Direct Payment Workflow — guide the user naturally through these steps:**

**Step 1 · Who is being paid?** Gather each recipient. For an existing Contra freelancer, use `search_freelancers` or `get_user_profile_by_username` to get their `userProfileId` and pass it as `userProfileId`. Otherwise pass the recipient's `email` together with `firstName` and `lastName` — Contra pays the existing account for that email, or invites the person if there is none. Each recipient also needs an `amount` (US dollars) and a short `title` describing what the payment is for.

**Step 2 · What is the payment called?** Ask for an overall `title` for the whole payment (e.g. "June contractor payouts").

**Step 3 · Which payment method?** Call `list_payment_methods` to get the user's saved payment methods for their client workspace. If there is only one, confirm it with the user. If there are multiple, ask which one to use.

Once all information is gathered, call this tool to prepare the draft. Show the returned `preview` to the user — including every recipient by name (and username or email), the per-recipient amounts, and the `paymentBreakdown` (subtotal, Contra fee, and processing fees) — and wait for explicit approval before calling `send_direct_payment_confirm`. For a recipient shown as `type: 'EMAIL'`, show its `note` and present `providedName` as the name the user gave, not as a confirmed Contra identity — the payment routes on the email address alone.

paymentMethodId.description: Saved payment method ID (PaymentMethodV2) from list_payment_methods.

amount.description: Amount to pay this recipient, in US dollars (e.g. 150.00). Must be greater than 0, a whole number of cents, and at most 1000000.

email.description: Recipient email address. Required if userProfileId is not provided. Contra pays the existing account for this email, or invites the person if there is none — firstName and lastName are always required with an email.

firstName.description: First name. Required when email is provided.

lastName.description: Last name. Required when email is provided.

title.description: Description of what this recipient is being paid for (e.g. "June retainer").

userProfileId.description: UserProfile ID of an existing Contra user. Use get_user_profile_by_username or search_freelancers to look this up. Alternative to email.

recipients.description: Recipients to pay. At least one is required.

returnUrl.description: Optional 3DS return URL. Defaults to CONTRA_MCP_BASE_URL/stripe-3ds-return when omitted.

contra_tools.name: send_direct_payment_confirm
contra_tools.description: Executes a prepared direct payment draft via createAndChargeDirectPayment, charging the selected payment method and paying every recipient. Only call this after the user has explicitly approved the preview returned by send_direct_payment_prepare. The draft is consumed by this call, so never retry it after an error — check list_client_transactions first to see whether the payment already went through. Always report the returned `status` to the user, which is one of: `SUCCEEDED` — the payment went through; `REQUIRES_ACTION` — the payment is NOT complete, surface `requiresAction.message` and, when present, `requiresAction.redirectToUrl` so the user can finish authenticating it; `FAILED` — the payment did NOT go through, tell the user so plainly, surface `charge.paymentErrorMessage`, and note that sending it requires a new send_direct_payment_prepare; `UNKNOWN` — the server returned no charge, so the outcome is indeterminate and the payment may or may not have been created. Tell the user the outcome is unconfirmed and check list_client_transactions before doing anything else. Only `SUCCEEDED` means the money moved — never describe any other status as a completed payment.

**Payment Link Creation Workflow — guide the user naturally through these steps:**

**Step 1 · What is this payment link for?** Ask for a title and description. The description supports markdown or plain text and will be shown to buyers.

**Step 2 · How much should it cost?** Ask for the price as a USD decimal string (e.g. "50.00"). Optionally ask if this should be a recurring payment — if so, collect a billing interval (unit and value, e.g. MONTH / 1 for monthly).

**Step 3 · Who covers the fees?** Contra charges a platform fee and a payment processing fee. Ask whether the buyer (PAYER) or the seller (RECIPIENT) should cover each fee. Explain the options clearly.

**Step 4 · Publish immediately?** Ask if the payment link should be published right away or saved as a draft.

**Step 5 · Optional associations.** Ask if the link should be attached to a product offering or productized service (both optional).

Once all information is gathered, call this tool to prepare the draft. Show the returned preview to the user and wait for explicit approval before calling `create_payment_link_confirm`.

public_opportunities.description:
About RedirHub
RedirHub helps businesses manage domain and URL redirects at scale: 301 redirects, HTTPS on redirected domains, branded links and website migrations. Our customers are SEO consultants, agencies and teams moving or consolidating websites.
Why we're hiring
People who find us through AI assistants (ChatGPT, Gemini, Perplexity) are already our best users. They sign up and set up a domain at a much higher rate than visitors from any other channel. But AI assistants still mention us far less often than they should, especially ChatGPT, and almost never for SEO and website-migration questions, which are our strongest use case. We want someone to fix that.

AI visibility tracking: an automated system that asks ChatGPT and Gemini 60 buyer questions on a schedule and records whether RedirHub is mentioned, our position, competitors and cited sources. You'll see the baseline on day one and measure your impact against it.
Product Facts: an internal library of verified, approved product facts (pricing, limits, SLA, infrastructure, features), so every claim you make is accurate.
llms.txt: a structured index of our site for AI models.
About 30 comparison pages already live (redirect.pizza, Cloudflare, urllo, redirection.io, Bitly, Short.io, Rebrandly, Dub and more), plus how-to guides and support docs.
Growth engineers who ship page changes quickly, and analytics that show AI-referred sign-ups.
We don't need another audit. We need someone to execute.
What you'll do
Get RedirHub into the third-party sources AI assistants cite: "best tools" lists and comparison articles, G2, Capterra, AlternativeTo, SaaSHub, Reddit and community threads, Q&A sites. Honestly earned, no spam, no fake reviews, no undisclosed paid posts.
Close the SEO and website-migration gap: plan and help produce the definitive guides AI should cite for questions like "how to preserve SEO during a site migration" or "how to redirect thousands of URLs".
Keep our own pages and llms.txt easy for AI to quote, using our approved Product Facts.
Report every two weeks on mentions, citations and AI-referred sign-ups, using our tracking data.
Engagement: part-time, about 10-15 hrs/week, ongoing. $30-60/hr depending on proven results.
You're likely a fit if you
Have measurably increased a brand's mentions or citations in AI assistants, ideally for B2B SaaS or a developer or marketing tool. Show us before-and-after evidence.
Know where LLM answers in our category pull from, and how to earn placements there honestly.
Do the hands-on work yourself: outreach to list owners and editors, listings, community participation, content briefs.
Write short, plain English and will tell us when something isn't worth doing.
How to apply (about 20 minutes)
Start your application with the word "Cited" so we know you read this far. Then😍 1. Your proof. One example where you increased a brand's visibility in AI answers: what you did, over what time period, and the before-and-after numbers. A screenshot or link helps.
Pick one question. Ask ChatGPT "How do I preserve SEO during a website migration?" or "Best redirect tool for website migration". Name 2-3 sources the answer relies on, and tell us how you'd get RedirHub into one of them.
Your first 30 days. The three actions you'd take first, and why each one matters.
Applications that skip these questions won't be reviewed.
Our process
